sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Tests for page loading retries
sections.what: Runs the checks for the lazy page loader, covering success, temporary failures, permanent failures, code errors, and error recognition.
sections.why: Keeps the retry behavior safe, since a bad change could hide real bugs or retry forever.
sections.watch_out: Each check asserts the exact number of attempts, so changing the retry count requires updating these numbers.

summary: Automated tests that check the retry logic for loading pages.
purpose: Proves that temporary download failures are retried, while real bugs are not hidden.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The tests cover the cases the retry logic must handle.
how: Runs five checks: a successful load, a temporary failure that recovers, a permanent failure that is reported after retries, a code error that is not retried, and the error recognizer for several messages.
inputs: Fake loaders and error messages built inside the tests.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each check.
risks: The tests depend on the exact error message wording, so a browser change could make real errors look different.
debug: Run the test file. If a check fails, compare the error message in the test with the message the browser actually produces.
